Here is the comprehensive design analysis of **futuredeluxe.com**: --- ## Grid Layout and Structure **Homepage layout:** The site follows a single-column continuous scroll on the homepage with a hero section at top, followed by a horizontal project carousel (not a traditional grid), then a philosophy/testimonial section, a contact CTA, and a four-column footer. **Work page grid:** The `/work/` page uses a flexbox-based post grid (`.is-layout-flex`) rather than CSS Grid. Cards are uniform in size with no hero/featured cards spanning multiple columns. The gap between items is `0.5em` for flex layouts and `1.25em` for grid layouts. Columns use a `2em` gap. **Card structure (HTML):** ```html

Client Name

Project Title

 ``` Each card is a single anchor wrapping an image and two headings. The entire card is clickable. Images use a 2:1 aspect ratio (`contain-intrinsic-size: 3000px 1500px`) with lazy loading. Text sits below the image, not overlaid. There is no visible border-radius on cards, no drop shadows on cards, and no explicit card background color -- cards inherit the page background, creating a borderless, floating feel. **What makes the grid modern:** The grid avoids visual "card" containers entirely. There are no borders, no box shadows, no background colors differentiating cards from the page. Items float in whitespace. This is the single biggest factor in creating the modern aesthetic -- the absence of container chrome. --- ## Typography - **Hero headline:** "Create the Future." -- large scale, approximately 36-42px (`--wp--preset--font-size--large: 36px`, `--wp--preset--font-size--x-large: 42px`) - **Body/subhead:** Medium size at 20px (`--wp--preset--font-size--medium`) - **Small text:** 13px (`--wp--preset--font-size--small`) - **Font family:** No explicit `@font-face` or Google Fonts link detected. The site appears to use a clean sans-serif system font stack, which itself contributes to the modern feel (fast loading, native rendering) - **Heading hierarchy:** H2 for client/brand name, H3/H4 for project title. The client name is treated as the primary label, project title as secondary - **No visible letter-spacing or text-transform declarations** in the extracted CSS, suggesting titles are written in their natural case rather than forced uppercase --- ## Color Usage The palette is extremely restrained: | Role | Color | Notes | |------|-------|-------| | Page background | White (`#ffffff`) | Clean, gallery-like | | Text | Black (`#000000`) | High contrast, no grays for primary text | | Primary accent | `#fe8076` | Coral/salmon -- used for hover borders, link states | | Tertiary | `#bdeece` | Mint green -- used for "Experiments" section | | Auxiliary | `#bda06d` | Gold/tan -- used for "News" section | | Blue | `#1e73be` | Accent, secondary | The key design decision: **color is reserved almost exclusively for interactive states and category coding.** The resting state of the page is black-on-white with no decorative color. Accent colors only appear on hover or as section identifiers. This creates a gallery/museum aesthetic where the project imagery provides all the color. --- ## Image and Media Presentation - **Thumbnails:** Large, landscape-oriented images at 2:1 aspect ratio. Full-width within their grid column - **Video on hover:** Videos have `data-play="hover"` attribute. A custom jQuery plugin (`hoverPlay()`) triggers autoplay when the cursor enters the card. This is the signature interaction -- static thumbnails come alive on hover - **Hero:** Uses an animated GIF (`frontpage_002-3.gif`) as background, not a video element. This avoids autoplay restrictions while still providing motion - **Lazy loading:** Images use native lazy loading for performance - **No overlays, filters, or color treatments** on thumbnails. The work speaks for itself without Instagram-style filters or dark overlays with text --- ## Navigation - **Structure:** Horizontal, four items: **Moving Image | Immersive | Research | Info** - **Position:** Fixed header. The nav wrapper has `pointer-events: none` (with pointer-events re-enabled on the actual links), creating a pass-through header that doesn't block scroll interactions - **Logo:** "FutureDeluxe" as a text/image link, top-left - **Mobile:** Duplicate nav structure exists for mobile (hamburger menu pattern) - **Skip link:** Accessibility skip-to-content link present but visually hidden - **Category labels on work page:** "Brand, Product, Campaign, Experience" -- filtering capability The navigation is notably minimal -- only 4 items. No dropdowns, no mega-menus. The categories on the work page provide secondary navigation/filtering. --- ## What Creates the "Modern Feel" Several specific design decisions combine: 1. **No card containers.** Items are images + text floating in whitespace. No borders, no shadows, no background cards. This is the single most impactful choice. 2. **Video-on-hover.** Static thumbnails that play video when hovered create a sense of life and interactivity without overwhelming the page. The `data-play="hover"` pattern is distinctly modern. 3. **Extreme color restraint.** Black, white, and one coral accent. The work's own colors dominate. The site acts as a neutral gallery frame. 4. **Generous whitespace.** Spacing tokens go up to `5.06rem` (80px). The breathing room between elements signals confidence and premium positioning. 5. **AOS scroll animations.** Elements animate in as you scroll (600ms duration, ease timing, 100px trigger offset). This creates a reveal rhythm rather than everything appearing at once. 6. **Minimal navigation.** Only 4 items. No utility nav, no search bar, no language selector. Radical simplification. 7. **Full-bleed imagery.** Images are large and dominant. Text is secondary. The ratio of image-to-text is heavily weighted toward visuals. 8. **System fonts / no decorative type.** Clean sans-serif without custom display fonts keeps the focus on content. 9. **Borderless everything.** Buttons have `border-radius: 9999px` (pill shape) but cards have no borders. The only border color change is the `#fe8076` coral on hover. 10. **Continuous scroll flow.** Sections blend into each other without hard dividers, horizontal rules, or background color changes. The page reads as one continuous surface. --- ## Hover States and Interactions - **Project cards:** Border color transitions to `#fe8076` (coral) on hover. Videos with `data-play="hover"` begin playing. No scale transform, no opacity change, no overlay - **Links:** `::after` pseudo-element animates with background color for underline effects - **Navigation links:** Underline animation on hover - **Buttons:** Pill-shaped (`border-radius: 9999px`) with padding `calc(.667em + 2px) calc(1.333em + 2px)` The hover philosophy is **subtle and functional** -- a color accent appears, video plays. There are no dramatic transforms, zooms, or parallax effects on cards. --- ## Spacing and Rhythm CSS custom property spacing scale: | Token | Value | |-------|-------| | `--spacing--20` | 0.44rem | | `--spacing--30` | 0.67rem | | `--spacing--40` | 1rem | | `--spacing--50` | 1.5rem | | `--spacing--60` | 2.25rem | | `--spacing--70` | 3.38rem | | `--spacing--80` | 5.06rem | This is a **geometric progression** (each step is roughly 1.5x the previous), creating natural visual rhythm. The flex gap of `0.5em` between cards is deliberately tight -- just enough separation to distinguish items without creating "card" isolation. The column gap of `2em` is significantly larger, creating clear column separation while maintaining tight vertical rhythm within columns. --- ## Footer Structure Four global office locations presented in equal columns: - **London, Los Angeles, Sydney, NYC** - Each with: street address (linked to Google Maps), email, phone, timezone - Social links: Instagram, LinkedIn, Vimeo - Copyright: "2026 FutureDeluxe" - Design credit to Luke Greenaway --- ## Summary: Key Takeaways for Your Portfolio The patterns most worth borrowing: 1. **Kill the card container** -- let thumbnails float in space with no border/shadow/background 2. **Video-on-hover** -- you already have Vimeo integration; triggering preview playback on hover would be high-impact 3. **Coral/amber accent on hover only** -- you already use `#FFB000` amber; reserving it strictly for hover states would increase its impact 4. **Tight grid gap, generous section spacing** -- cards close together (0.5em), sections far apart (5rem+) 5. **2:1 landscape thumbnails** -- consistent aspect ratio across all project cards creates visual order 6. **Minimal nav** -- your 5-item nav (WORK | INFO | PHOTO | EXPLORE | chat) is already close to their 4-item pattern 7. **AOS-style scroll reveal** -- entrance animations as cards scroll into view add perceived polish

## Found Studio (found-studio.com) -- Design Pattern Analysis

### 1. Overall Design Philosophy

Found Studio's website embodies a **premium editorial aesthetic** -- more digital magazine than traditional portfolio grid. The site prioritizes storytelling and breathing room over density. Every design decision reinforces the positioning as a luxury motion design studio. The word that best captures it: **restraint**.

---

### 2. Color Scheme and Contrast

**Homepage / Work index:**
- **Background:** Deep black (`#0a0000` or near-black) -- creates an immersive, cinematic environment
- **Text:** White and light gray -- high contrast against the dark background
- **No accent colors** -- the studio lets project imagery provide all the color. The UI itself is nearly monochrome.

**Project detail pages:**
- **Background:** White/light -- switches to a clean white background for case studies
- **Text:** Black/dark gray body copy
- **This contrast flip** (dark index, light detail pages) is a deliberate design choice: the work index feels like a gallery or cinema lobby (dark, atmospheric), while the case study pages feel like a printed monograph (clean, readable, editorial).

**Key takeaway:** The color palette is essentially black, white, and gray. Zero accent colors in the chrome. This forces all visual interest onto the project imagery itself.

---

### 3. Navigation Patterns

**Primary navigation:** Horizontal, minimal, five items only:
- **Work | Reels | News | Perspectives | Contact**

**Characteristics:**
- Sans-serif typeface, likely a geometric or grotesque family
- Lightweight, generous letter-spacing
- Contact info (phone + email) visible in the header -- unusual for a creative studio, signals accessibility
- Logo as home link (left-aligned)
- No hamburger menu on desktop; the five items fit comfortably
- Navigation remains consistent across all pages (no variation per section)

**Breadcrumb navigation** on inner pages: `Home > Work > [Project Name]` -- provides structural orientation without visual clutter. Uses Schema.org markup for SEO.

**No sticky/fixed navigation** appears to be used -- the nav scrolls away, giving maximum screen real estate to content.

---

### 4. Work Index Page (Grid Layout)

**Structure:**
- Projects are presented as a **vertical feed** of large thumbnail cards
- Each card contains: **thumbnail image + project title + subtitle/tagline**
- The layout is closer to a **single-column or two-column masonry** approach than a dense multi-column grid
- Filtering system with categories: **People, Process, Stories** -- minimal taxonomy, not overwhelming

**Card design:**
- Large-scale imagery dominates each card
- Project title below the image in clean sans-serif
- Subtitle/tagline in smaller, lighter weight text
- No borders, no shadows, no rounded corners -- images sit directly on the dark background
- Generous spacing between cards -- each project gets room to breathe

**Content on index:** Approximately 12 projects visible (Specsavers, Orluna Carbolite, Bentley, Forward Festival 2025, London Craft Week, Ralph Lauren Romance, CCEP, Channel 4, Invisible, L'Oreal, Toblerone, Vessel).

**Key takeaway:** The grid is NOT a dense Pinterest-style masonry. It is more like a curated editorial selection -- fewer items, larger presentation, more whitespace. Quality over quantity.

---

### 5. Individual Project Page Structure

This is where the site truly excels. Every project page follows a consistent but flexible template:

**Content flow (top to bottom):**

1. **Project Title** (H1) -- large, bold, sans-serif
2. **Subtitle/Tagline** (H2) -- campaign name or concept line (e.g., "Made to Move You" for Bentley, "A Little More Edge" for Toblerone)
3. **Introduction paragraph** -- 2-4 sentences establishing context. Editorial tone. Left-aligned body copy.
4. **Themed sections** -- each with:
   - **Section header** in UPPERCASE (e.g., "SHAPE", "SENSATION", "PROCESS", "INGREDIENTS", "ABSTRACTIONS", "COLOUR", "PROMOS")
   - **Descriptive paragraph** explaining the creative approach
   - **Image group** -- varies per section (see media patterns below)
5. **Credits section** -- structured key-value pairs
6. **Awards** (if applicable) -- listed below credits
7. **Press mentions** -- linked external coverage
8. **"More work" section** -- 3 related projects with thumbnails
9. **Footer**

**Key takeaway:** The project page is a **narrative journey**, not a media dump. Each section tells a chapter of the creative story. Text and media alternate in a deliberate rhythm.

---

### 6. Media Presentation on Project Pages

Found uses a **limited vocabulary of media layouts**, applied flexibly per project:

| Layout Type | Description | Usage |
|-------------|-------------|-------|
| **Full-width single** | One image spanning the full content width | Hero shots, key frames |
| **Two-column pair** | Two images side by side (50/50 split) | Comparison, ingredient pairs, process shots |
| **2x2 grid** | Four images in a square grid | Detail explorations, texture studies |
| **Stacked singles** | Multiple full-width images in sequence | Sequential narrative moments |

**Characteristics:**
- **No carousels or sliders** -- all media is visible without interaction
- **No lightbox popups** -- images are presented at their intended size
- **No captions** on images -- the section text above provides context
- **No rounded corners** on media
- **No decorative borders or frames**
- **Aspect ratios** vary by project but tend toward cinematic (wider than tall) for hero shots and closer to square for detail/texture images
- **Video embeds** are not prominent in the HTML -- the studio appears to link to Vimeo for full video playback rather than embedding inline players

**Key takeaway:** Media presentation is deliberately simple. The images do the talking. No UI chrome competes with the visuals.

---

### 7. Typography Hierarchy

**Font family:** Sans-serif throughout (likely a single family with weight variations -- possibly Neue Haas Grotesk, Suisse, Graphik, or similar contemporary grotesque).

| Element | Treatment |
|---------|-----------|
| **Project title (H1)** | Large, bold/medium weight, generous size |
| **Subtitle (H2)** | Lighter weight, slightly smaller than H1 |
| **Section headers** | ALL CAPS, medium weight, moderate size, generous letter-spacing |
| **Body copy** | Regular weight, comfortable reading size (~16-18px equivalent), generous line-height (~1.6-1.8) |
| **Credits labels** | Small, likely bold or medium weight |
| **Credits values** | Small, regular weight, linked (underline on hover) |
| **Navigation** | Medium weight, moderate size, generous letter-spacing |

**Key characteristics:**
- **Single typeface** used throughout -- unity and simplicity
- **Weight and size** do all the hierarchical work (no color differentiation, no decorative fonts)
- **Generous line-height** on body copy -- contributes to the "breathing" feel
- **Letter-spacing** on uppercase elements and navigation -- adds airiness

---

### 8. Spacing and Rhythm

This is perhaps the single most impactful design pattern on the site.

**Vertical spacing:**
- **Very large gaps** between sections (estimated 80-120px or more)
- **Consistent padding** within sections between text and media
- **Asymmetric rhythm** -- the gap after a media block before the next section header is larger than the gap between a section header and its body text. This creates visual "paragraphs" at the section level.

**Horizontal spacing:**
- Content appears constrained to a **max-width container** (likely 1200-1400px)
- Body text may use an even narrower max-width for comfortable reading line length
- **Full-width images** respect the container but may extend slightly wider for visual emphasis

**Key takeaway:** The spacing is what makes it feel "clean." Most portfolios pack content tightly. Found does the opposite -- every element has room to breathe. The whitespace is not empty; it is a design element carrying the same weight as the content.

---

### 9. Credits Section

A consistent pattern across all project pages:

```
Client:     [Name, linked]
Agency:     [Name, linked]
Audio:      [Name, linked]
Awards:     [Award name + category]
Press:      [Publication, linked]
```

**Characteristics:**
- Simple **key-value pair layout**
- Collaborator names are **hyperlinked** to their sites
- Minimal styling -- no boxes, no cards, no icons
- Positioned near the bottom, after the narrative content
- Social sharing links (Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn) adjacent to credits

---

### 10. "More Work" Related Projects Section

Every project page ends with:

**"More work"** heading + **"View all"** link

Three project cards displayed horizontally, each showing:
- Thumbnail image
- Project title
- Subtitle/tagline

This serves as both **related content discovery** and **portfolio navigation**. It keeps the user in a browsing loop without requiring them to return to the index.

---

### 11. What Makes It Feel "Clean and Modern"

Synthesizing all the patterns above, the "clean and modern" feeling comes from these specific, replicable decisions:

1. **Monochrome UI chrome** -- the interface itself has zero color. All color comes from project imagery.

2. **Single typeface** -- one font family, hierarchy through weight/size/case only. No decorative fonts, no serif/sans-serif mixing.

3. **Extreme whitespace** -- sections are separated by generous vertical gaps. Content never feels cramped.

4. **No decorative elements** -- no borders, shadows, rounded corners, gradients, icons, or ornamental graphics anywhere.

5. **Dark/light context switch** -- dark background for browsing/discovery, white background for reading/studying. Each context is optimized for its purpose.

6. **Editorial content flow** -- project pages tell a story with chapters, not just display a grid of images. The text-media-text rhythm gives meaning to the visuals.

7. **Restrained media vocabulary** -- only 3-4 layout types for media (full-width, two-column, 2x2 grid, stacked). No sliders, carousels, lightboxes, or parallax effects.

8. **Flat hierarchy in navigation** -- five items, no dropdowns, no mega-menus. You can see everything at once.

9. **Linked credits** -- collaborators are credited and linked, but in a quiet, structured format that does not compete with the work.

10. **No animation gimmicks** -- the site does not rely on scroll-triggered animations, parallax, or complex transitions to feel modern. The modernity comes from proportion, spacing, and restraint.

---

### 12. Structural Summary for Reference

```
HOMEPAGE
  [Dark bg]
  Nav: Logo | Work | Reels | News | Perspectives | Contact | Phone | Email
  Hero: Tagline + arrow
  Mission: "Intelligent Beauty" philosophy
  Featured work grid
  Footer: Address, socials, newsletter

WORK INDEX
  [Dark bg]
  Filter: People | Process | Stories
  Project cards (large thumbnails + title + subtitle)
  Generous spacing between cards

PROJECT DETAIL
  [White bg]
  Breadcrumb: Home > Work > [Name]
  H1: Client name
  H2: Campaign/project tagline
  Intro paragraph (2-4 sentences)
  
  [Repeating section pattern:]
    SECTION HEADER (uppercase)
    Description paragraph
    Media group (full-width, 2-col, or 2x2 grid)
  
  Credits (key-value, linked)
  Awards + Press
  Share links
  
  "More work" (3 related project cards)
  Footer

FOOTER (all pages)
  Logo
  Address + map link
  Phone + email
  Social: Instagram, Twitter, Vimeo, LinkedIn, Facebook, Behance
  Newsletter signup
  Legal links
```

This analysis should give you a detailed blueprint of the design patterns that make Found Studio's site feel premium, clean, and editorially driven. The core lesson is that restraint and spacing do more work than any individual design element.

### 7.1 Magazine Editorial Structure
Each project reads like a feature article in a design publication. There is a clear narrative arc (brief, concept, execution, process) with crafted headings that feel editorial rather than functional.

### 7.2 Text-Visual Rhythm
The alternation between short conceptual text blocks and large image carousels creates a breathing rhythm. You read, then you see. Read, then see. This is pacing -- it prevents both wall-of-text fatigue and wall-of-images meaninglessness.

Instead of "Overview", "Process", "Deliverables" (boring, functional), Tendril uses evocative headings: "Made by Metal", "Moments on the living gridiron", "Surreal Brand Worldbuilding". These headings do double duty as creative statements and section markers.

Carousels with 10-20 images per section communicate **depth of craft**. A project with 50+ images across multiple carousels says "we produced an enormous amount of high-quality work" without needing to say it.

### 7.5 Process & R&D as a First-Class Section
Every project includes a dedicated process section. This is not an afterthought -- it is positioned as a major content block with its own large carousel. This signals to potential clients: "we think deeply, we explore broadly."

### 7.6 Client Quotes at Peak Position
When present, client testimonials sit between the hero and the body -- maximum visibility, maximum credibility.

### 7.7 The "Next Project" Chain
The bottom of every page flows directly into the next project with a large visual preview. This creates a **gallery walk** experience -- visitors naturally keep exploring rather than returning to the index.

### 7.8 Clean Hero Without Text Overlay
The hero image is never obscured by text. Title and category sit above it. The image gets full visual authority. This respects the craft of the work being shown.

### 7.9 Collapsible Credits
Full production credits are available but hidden by default. This respects both the team (full attribution) and the viewer (clean page).

### 7.10 Restraint
Perhaps most importantly: the site does almost nothing flashy. No parallax. No scroll-jacking. No animated counters. No loading animations (visible in markup). The work carries the page. This restraint is what makes it feel premium.

[NAV BAR]                           -- Work | Studio | Careers | Contact

[CLIENT | PROJECT NAME]             -- Large heading, clean sans-serif
[Category Tag]                      -- Small, subdued

[HERO IMAGE]                        -- Full-bleed, 16:9+, no overlay

[IMAGE CAROUSEL]                    -- 5-20 images, full-width

[SECTION HEADING]                   -- Next narrative beat
[BODY TEXT]
[IMAGE CAROUSEL]

[BODY TEXT]
[LARGE CAROUSEL]                    -- 10-20 exploration images

[CREDITS]                           -- Collapsible, organized by department
[NEXT PROJECT]                      -- Full-width preview thumbnail + title

[FOOTER]
```

### 7.8 Clean Hero Without Text Overlay
The hero image is never obscured by text. Title and category sit above it. The image gets full visual authority. This respects the craft of the work being shown.

### 7.9 Collapsible Credits
Full production credits are available but hidden by default. This respects both the team (full attribution) and the viewer (clean page).

### 7.10 Restraint
Perhaps most importantly: the site does almost nothing flashy. No parallax. No scroll-jacking. No animated counters. No loading animations (visible in markup). The work carries the page. This restraint is what makes it feel premium.

---

## Summary: Tendril's Case Study Page Template

```
[NAV BAR]                           -- Work | Studio | Careers | Contact

[CLIENT | PROJECT NAME]             -- Large heading, clean sans-serif
[Category Tag]                      -- Small, subdued

[HERO IMAGE]                        -- Full-bleed, 16:9+, no overlay

[CLIENT QUOTE]                      -- Optional, high-impact position

[INTRO PARAGRAPH]                   -- 1-2 paragraphs, sets the brief

[SECTION HEADING]                   -- Evocative, conceptual
[BODY TEXT]                         -- 2-4 sentences
[IMAGE CAROUSEL]                    -- 5-20 images, full-width

[SECTION HEADING]                   -- Next narrative beat
[BODY TEXT]
[IMAGE CAROUSEL]

... repeat 3-6 times ...

[PROCESS & R&D]                     -- Dedicated section
[BODY TEXT]
[LARGE CAROUSEL]                    -- 10-20 exploration images

[CREDITS]                           -- Collapsible, organized by department
[NEXT PROJECT]                      -- Full-width preview thumbnail + title

[FOOTER]
```

This template is worth studying for your own project pages. The key takeaway is that exceptional case study pages tell a **story** (not just show images), maintain a **rhythm** (text-visual alternation), and exercise **restraint** (let the work speak).

## Reference Analysis: Patterns You're Drawn To

Across all 5 references, these patterns repeat consistently:

| Pattern | Pentagram | Electric Theatre | Future Deluxe | Tendril | Found Studio |
|---------|-----------|-----------------|---------------|---------|--------------|
| Monochrome chrome (no accent in UI) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Single typeface | ✓ | ✓ (Proxima Nova) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| No card containers (no borders/shadows) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

| Video-on-hover thumbnails | — | — | ✓ | — | — |
| Collapsible credits | — | — | — | ✓ | — |
| Dark index / Light detail | — | — | — | — | ✓ |

## Gap Analysis: Your Site vs. References

### Where you already match:
- Dark monochrome background (your `#141414` = Found Studio's approach)
- Minimal nav (5 items — close to the 4-item pattern)
- Video-on-hover thumbnails (like Future Deluxe, you already have this)
- "Next Project" navigation on detail pages
- Generous spacing via golden ratio Fibonacci system

### Where you diverge significantly:

**1. Too many typefaces (4 vs. 1)**
- You: Inter + DM Sans + Open Sans + Lora
- Every reference: single font family, hierarchy through weight/size only
- **Suggestion:** Consolidate to Inter (already your primary) with weight variants. Drop DM Sans and Open Sans. Keep Lora only for the one hero quote if you want that editorial contrast.

**2. Card containers have too much UI chrome**
- Your `ProjectCard` has hover opacity shifts, saturation filters, background shadows
- References: thumbnails float in space with zero decoration. No `boxShadow: 'inset 0 0 0 1px #141414'`, no `filter: saturate(0.6) brightness(0.85)`
- **Suggestion:** Let thumbnails sit at full brightness/saturation by default. Remove inset shadows. Let the dark background be the only "frame."

**3. Project detail pages lack editorial depth**
- Your `ProjectDetailContent` is: hero video → metadata → description → breakdowns → credits → nav
- Tendril/Found pattern: hero → intro paragraph → **3-6 themed narrative sections** each with heading + text + media group → process section → collapsible credits → next project
- **Suggestion:** This is the biggest opportunity. Your projects have `lightingIntent`, `challenge`, `approach`, `reference` fields — these could become editorial sections with evocative headings instead of a flat metadata dump.

**4. Grid uniformity**
- Your LadderGrid uses staggered animation with varied visual weight
- References: uniform grid, equal column widths, consistent aspect ratios
- **Suggestion:** Consider a cleaner 2 or 3-column uniform grid where every card gets equal visual weight. The stagger animation is nice but adds visual complexity the references avoid.

**5. Amber accent is overused**
- References use accent color ONLY on hover/interactive states
- Your `#d4a853` / `#FFB000` appears in multiple static contexts
- **Suggestion:** Reserve amber strictly for hover underlines and interactive affordances. Never as resting-state decoration.

**6. Missing the dark→light context switch**
- Found Studio uses dark bg for browsing, white bg for reading project details
- Your site is dark everywhere
- **Suggestion:** Consider switching project detail pages to a light background. This creates reading comfort for the editorial text and makes project imagery pop differently.

---

## Concrete Suggestions (Priority Order)

### High Impact — Design Alignment

1. **Redesign project detail pages as editorial narratives** (Tendril/Found model)
   - Turn `lightingIntent` → evocative section heading + paragraph
   - Turn `challenge` → section heading + paragraph + media
   - Turn `approach` → section heading + paragraph + media
   - Add collapsible credits toggle
   - Use full-width image sections between narrative blocks

2. **Consolidate to 1-2 fonts max**
   - Inter for everything. Lora italic for one pull quote. Drop DM Sans + Open Sans.

3. **Strip card chrome**
   - Remove `boxShadow`, `filter: saturate()`, `brightness()` from thumbnail resting state
   - Full brightness, full saturation by default
   - Keep hover-to-play video (that's your Future Deluxe moment)

4. **Uniform grid**

### Medium Impact — Polish

5. **Reserve amber for interaction only** — remove from static elements

7. **Add client quotes** to project pages where available (Tendril pattern — between hero and intro)

8. **Simplify project card text** — title only on grid, save description for detail page (Electric Theatre pattern)

11. **Conceptual section headings** — "Problems of Light" is a great start; extend this voice into per-project section titles instead of generic labels

Your site is technically excellent (A- code quality) but **over-designed at the chrome level and under-designed at the content level**. The references succeed by stripping UI to nothing and investing everything in editorial storytelling on project pages. The biggest win would be transforming your project detail pages from metadata displays into magazine-quality narratives — you already have the data fields to do it.

- `fadeUp`: 0.7s ease-out, staggered (0-400ms delays)
- `scrollFloat`: Scroll indicator chevron (2.8s infinite)
- `typingPulse`: Chat typing dots (opacity 0.3→1, scale 1→1.15)
- `chatMessageIn`: Chat messages (300ms, 13px translate)

**View Transitions (Page Crossfades):**
- **Root content**: 500ms fade + scale (0.98 out, 1.02 in)
- **Navigation/footer**: 400ms fade only (stays anchored)
- **Hero reel**: 400ms fade only (prevents white flash from Vimeo iframe)
- **Background**: Dark canvas `#141414` prevents white bleed-through

**Hover Interactions:**
- `.nav-link`: Opacity 1 → 0.6 (reversed: bright by default, dims on hover)
- `.section-header-highlight`: Opacity 0.5 → 1 (light table effect: dim by default, reveals on hover)
- `.button-arrow`: Opacity 0.5 → 1 + `translateX(4px)`

### 3. **layout.tsx** (176 lines)
Root layout that configures fonts, metadata, and view transitions:

**Fonts:**
- **Inter**: 400/500/600 weights (nav, headings) — `--font-inter` CSS variable
- **Open Sans**: 300/400 weights (body text) — `--font-open-sans`
- **Lora**: 400 normal + italic (editorial serif for hero statement) — `--font-lora`
- **DM Sans**: 400/500 (utility) — `--font-dm-sans`

**Head Optimizations:**
- Preconnects to Vimeo CDN (`player.vimeo.com`, `i.vimeocdn.com`, `f.vimeocdn.com`, `vod-progressive.akamaized.net`)
- Inline dark CSS to prevent white flash on reload
- Schema.org structured data (Person type, job title, alumni, skills)

**Body:**
- Background: `#141414`
- Text color: `#a0a0a0`
- View transitions wrapper (cinematic page crossfades)
- Skip link for keyboard accessibility

### 4. **page.tsx** (Homepage, 241 lines)
Hero + project grid layout with scroll-driven animations:

**Hero Section:**
- **Height**: 50vh mobile / 70vh desktop
- **Statement**: "Sixteen years. Feature films, commercials, real-time engines—each frame a problem of light solved in pixels. This is the work."
- **Typography**: Lora italic, `#a0a0a0`, 22-38px (clamp), 1.2 line height
- **Animation**: Fade-in + translateY on mount (550ms cubic-bezier), reversible on scroll

**Scroll-Driven DOM Updates:**
1. **Scroll Indicator** (chevron + "Scroll" text): Fades 0→1 over first 300px scroll
2. **Intro Text**: Fades at 600-800px scroll (moves under navigation)
3. **Gradient Overlay**: Darkens as content scrolls under nav (prevents readability loss)
4. **Grid**: LadderGrid with adapted project order (if visitor archetype detected with confidence > 0.5)

**Styling:**
- Hero padding: `clamp(102px, 10.2vw + 34px, 170px)` (Pentagram-style golden ratio)
- Grid padding: `var(--side-padding)` = `clamp(24px, 3vw, 80px)`
- Max width: `var(--max-content-width)` = 1600px

### 5. **Navigation.tsx** (496 lines)
Fixed navigation with scroll-driven background opacity and mobile menu:

**Desktop Layout:**
- Logo + 4 nav links + chat bubble
- Links: Work | Photo | Process | About | 💬
- Font: Inter, 18-21px, 500 weight, 0.10em letter-spacing (uppercase)

**Scroll Behavior:**
- **Hero reel pages** (home + project pages): Navigation background fades `transparent → rgba(20,20,20,1)` as user scrolls and hero video fades
- **Calculation**: Synchronized with page.tsx scroll logic (hero height × 0.7, fadeStart at 30% for projects / calculated for homepage)

**Interactive Features:**
- **Single-click chat icon**: Opens ChatBot overlay
- **Double-click chat icon**: Reveals Tools overlay (Easter Egg)
- **Mobile menu**: Hamburger toggle, fullscreen overlay, 44px min touch targets
- **Focus trap**: Sets `inert` on main content when mobile menu is open

**Mobile:**
- Hamburger + chat icons (44px targets)
- Menu scales 36px → 72px (clamp responsive)
- Close button in top-right

**Styling:**
- Navigation always uses `viewTransitionName: 'navigation'` (fade-only page transitions)
- Text color: `var(--text-primary)` (`#e8e8e8`)
- Hover opacity: Dims to 60%

---

All files use a cohesive design system: golden ratio spacing, dark theme with warm gold accent, responsive typography via `clamp()`, and performance-optimized scroll animations. The architecture prioritizes accessibility (reduced motion, keyboard navigation, ARIA labels) and cinematic page transitions.

## Current State
- Dark theme (#141414), 4 fonts (Inter, DM Sans, Open Sans, Lora), golden ratio spacing
- 2-column staggered LadderGrid with scroll animations, hover-to-play video thumbnails
- Project detail page: hero video → metadata → description → collapsible "Project Details" → breakdowns → related work → prev/next nav
- VideoThumbnail: 60% opacity + desaturated at rest, full brightness on hover
- ProjectCard: title (Lora italic) + gridDescription + client below thumbnail
- 13 projects, all have lightingIntent, challenge, approach, reference, credits, technologies, responsibilities populated

## Target State (from references)
Design changes organized by priority:

### 1. Project Detail Page → Editorial Narrative (Tendril/Found model)
Current: flat metadata dump with collapsible details
Target: magazine-style editorial with narrative sections

New structure:
```
[PROJECT TYPE TAG]          -- small, uppercase, dim (keep existing)
[TITLE]                     -- change from Lora italic to Inter clean sans-serif
[METADATA: Year • Client • Studio]  -- keep existing
[MY ROLE + RESPONSIBILITIES] -- keep existing

[HERO VIDEO]                -- keep existing EmbeddedVideoPlayer

[DESCRIPTION]               -- make full-width, larger text, more editorial

[NARRATIVE SECTIONS - ALWAYS VISIBLE, NOT COLLAPSIBLE:]
  INTENT section heading + lightingIntent text
  CHALLENGE section heading + challenge text  
  APPROACH section heading + approach text
  REFERENCE section heading + reference text

[TECHNOLOGIES]              -- NEW: display as a clean inline list

[CREDITS]                   -- collapsible toggle (Tendril pattern)

[RELATED WORK]              -- upgrade: show 3 cards with thumbnails (Found pattern), not just text links
[NEXT PROJECT]              -- full-width thumbnail preview (Tendril pattern) replacing small prev/next text links
```

- Remove the collapsible "Project Details" toggle — show Intent/Challenge/Approach/Reference as always-visible editorial sections
- Each section gets an uppercase heading + body text, full-width, with generous spacing between
- Credits remain collapsible (Tendril pattern)
- Related work shows thumbnail cards instead of text-only links
- Next project becomes a prominent full-width card with thumbnail
- Remove prev project link (forward-only flow like Tendril)
- Section spacing: use --space-lg (89px) between major sections

Current: 4 fonts (Inter, DM Sans, Open Sans, Lora)
Target: Inter as primary for everything, Lora only for the homepage hero quote

- layout.tsx: Remove DM_Sans import, keep Open_Sans only if needed as fallback
- ProjectCard title: change from Lora italic to Inter 400
- ProjectDetailContent title: change from Lora italic to Inter 400
- All body text: Inter instead of Open Sans
- Footer: Inter instead of DM Sans references
- Keep Lora ONLY for the homepage hero statement italic quote

### 3. Strip Card Chrome (Electric Theatre/Future Deluxe pattern)
Current: VideoThumbnail at 60% opacity, desaturated, with inset box-shadow
Target: Full brightness/saturation at rest, no inset shadows

- Remove `boxShadow: 'inset 0 0 0 1px #141414'` from both mobile and desktop
- Change resting opacity from 0.60 to 0.85 (subtle dim, not dramatic)
- Change resting filter from `saturate(0.6) brightness(0.85)` to `saturate(0.85) brightness(0.95)` (subtle, not washed out)
- Keep hover state at full 1.0 opacity and full saturation

### 4. Simplify Project Card Text (Electric Theatre pattern)
Current: title (Lora italic) + gridDescription + client
Target: title (Inter, clean) + client only. No description on grid.

- Remove gridDescription display from cards
- Title: Inter 400 (not Lora italic), slightly smaller
- Client: keep as small uppercase metadata below

Current: #d4a853 amber used in some places
Target: Reserve amber ONLY for hover/interactive states

Target: increase to 120px between major sections on project detail pages

data.prompt:
You are a software architect planning a major visual redesign of a Next.js 16 portfolio site (josephibrahim.com). Based on reference site analysis (Pentagram, Electric Theatre, Future Deluxe, Tendril, Found Studio), here are the changes needed. Design a detailed, phased implementation plan.

## Current State
- Dark theme (#141414), 4 fonts (Inter, DM Sans, Open Sans, Lora), golden ratio spacing
- 2-column staggered LadderGrid with scroll animations, hover-to-play video thumbnails
- Project detail page: hero video → metadata → description → collapsible "Project Details" → breakdowns → related work → prev/next nav
- VideoThumbnail: 60% opacity + desaturated at rest, full brightness on hover
- ProjectCard: title (Lora italic) + gridDescription + client below thumbnail
- 13 projects, all have lightingIntent, challenge, approach, reference, credits, technologies, responsibilities populated

## Target State (from references)
Design changes organized by priority:

### 1. Project Detail Page → Editorial Narrative (Tendril/Found model)
Current: flat metadata dump with collapsible details
Target: magazine-style editorial with narrative sections

New structure:
```
[PROJECT TYPE TAG]          -- small, uppercase, dim (keep existing)
[TITLE]                     -- change from Lora italic to Inter clean sans-serif
[METADATA: Year • Client • Studio]  -- keep existing
[MY ROLE + RESPONSIBILITIES] -- keep existing

[HERO VIDEO]                -- keep existing EmbeddedVideoPlayer

[DESCRIPTION]               -- make full-width, larger text, more editorial

[NARRATIVE SECTIONS - ALWAYS VISIBLE, NOT COLLAPSIBLE:]
  INTENT section heading + lightingIntent text
  CHALLENGE section heading + challenge text  
  APPROACH section heading + approach text
  REFERENCE section heading + reference text

[TECHNOLOGIES]              -- NEW: display as a clean inline list

[CREDITS]                   -- collapsible toggle (Tendril pattern)

[RELATED WORK]              -- upgrade: show 3 cards with thumbnails (Found pattern), not just text links
[NEXT PROJECT]              -- full-width thumbnail preview (Tendril pattern) replacing small prev/next text links
```

Key changes:
- Remove the collapsible "Project Details" toggle — show Intent/Challenge/Approach/Reference as always-visible editorial sections
- Each section gets an uppercase heading + body text, full-width, with generous spacing between
- Credits remain collapsible (Tendril pattern)
- Related work shows thumbnail cards instead of text-only links
- Next project becomes a prominent full-width card with thumbnail
- Remove prev project link (forward-only flow like Tendril)
- Section spacing: use --space-lg (89px) between major sections

### 2. Typography Consolidation (All references use 1 font)
Current: 4 fonts (Inter, DM Sans, Open Sans, Lora)
Target: Inter as primary for everything, Lora only for the homepage hero quote

Changes:
- layout.tsx: Remove DM_Sans import, keep Open_Sans only if needed as fallback
- ProjectCard title: change from Lora italic to Inter 400
- ProjectDetailContent title: change from Lora italic to Inter 400
- All body text: Inter instead of Open Sans
- Footer: Inter instead of DM Sans references
- Keep Lora ONLY for the homepage hero statement italic quote

### 3. Strip Card Chrome (Electric Theatre/Future Deluxe pattern)
Current: VideoThumbnail at 60% opacity, desaturated, with inset box-shadow
Target: Full brightness/saturation at rest, no inset shadows

Changes in VideoThumbnail.tsx:
- Remove `boxShadow: 'inset 0 0 0 1px #141414'` from both mobile and desktop
- Change resting opacity from 0.60 to 0.85 (subtle dim, not dramatic)
- Change resting filter from `saturate(0.6) brightness(0.85)` to `saturate(0.85) brightness(0.95)` (subtle, not washed out)
- Keep hover state at full 1.0 opacity and full saturation

### 4. Simplify Project Card Text (Electric Theatre pattern)
Current: title (Lora italic) + gridDescription + client
Target: title (Inter, clean) + client only. No description on grid.

Changes in ProjectCard.tsx:
- Remove gridDescription display from cards
- Title: Inter 400 (not Lora italic), slightly smaller
- Client: keep as small uppercase metadata below
- This makes cards cleaner and saves description for detail pages

### 5. Accent Color Discipline
Current: #d4a853 amber used in some places
Target: Reserve amber ONLY for hover/interactive states

Review globals.css and components for any static (non-hover) uses of --accent color and remove them.

### 6. Section Spacing Increase
Current: --space-lg (89px) between sections
Target: increase to 120px between major sections on project detail pages

Add a new CSS variable --space-section: 120px for project detail page section gaps.

## Implementation Order
1. Typography consolidation (layout.tsx, globals.css) — foundational, affects everything
2. Project detail page redesign (ProjectDetailContent.tsx) — biggest visual change
3. Strip card chrome (VideoThumbnail.tsx) — quick win
4. Simplify card text (ProjectCard.tsx) — quick win
5. Accent color audit (globals.css, components) — cleanup pass
6. Spacing tuning (globals.css) — final polish

## Files to modify:
- `app/layout.tsx` — remove DM Sans, adjust font usage
- `app/globals.css` — add --space-section, minor variable changes
- `components/ProjectDetailContent.tsx` — major rewrite to editorial layout
- `components/ProjectCard.tsx` — simplify to title + client only, Inter font
- `components/VideoThumbnail.tsx` — raise resting opacity/saturation, remove box-shadow
- `components/Footer.tsx` — check for DM Sans references

## Constraints:
- Do NOT touch LadderGrid.tsx stagger/scroll animation — keep the golden ratio grid
- Do NOT touch Navigation.tsx
- Do NOT touch the perception system
- Do NOT touch HeroReel or homepage hero statement (keep Lora italic there)
- Keep all existing functionality (hover-to-play, scroll animations, view transitions)
- Keep dark theme (#141414)
- This is a VISUAL ONLY redesign — no new features, no data model changes

Provide a detailed implementation plan with specific code changes per file.

**Goal:** Align josephibrahim.com with the shared patterns across all references while keeping existing functionality (hover-to-play, scroll animations, perception system, dark theme).

---

**Why:** Every reference site uses a single font family. We have 4.

**Changes:**
- `app/layout.tsx` — Remove `DM_Sans` import + variable. Remove `Open_Sans` import + variable after all references updated.

**Files:** layout.tsx, ProjectDetailContent.tsx, ProjectCard.tsx, ChatBot.tsx, ChatProjectCard.tsx, Footer.tsx, info/page.tsx, process/page.tsx, process/[slug]/page.tsx, photo/page.tsx, gen-ai/page.tsx, SearchBar.tsx, ToolsOverlay.tsx, AccordionCategory.tsx, RotatingRole.tsx, ProjectGrid.tsx, CustomCursor.tsx, ProcessThumbnail.tsx, og-vfx-frame/page.tsx

---

## Phase 2: Project Detail Page → Editorial Narrative

**Why:** Biggest visual gap vs references. Current page is a flat metadata dump with collapsible details. Tendril/Found use magazine-style editorial sections.

**File:** `components/ProjectDetailContent.tsx` (major rewrite)

**New structure:**
```
PROJECT TYPE TAG (keep)
TITLE — change from Lora italic → Inter clean
METADATA LINE (keep)
MY ROLE + RESPONSIBILITIES (keep)
HERO VIDEO (keep)
DESCRIPTION — full-width, larger text

── EDITORIAL SECTIONS (always visible, NOT collapsible) ──
INTENT heading + lightingIntent text
CHALLENGE heading + challenge text
APPROACH heading + approach text
REFERENCE heading + reference text

TECHNOLOGIES — new inline list display
CREDITS — own collapsible toggle (Tendril pattern)

RELATED WORK — 3 thumbnail cards in grid (Found pattern)
NEXT PROJECT — full-width thumbnail card (Tendril pattern, forward-only)
```

**Key changes:**
- Remove collapsible "Project Details" → show all 4 narrative sections always visible
- Each section: uppercase label + body text, full-width, 120px spacing between
- Credits get their own collapsible toggle
- Related work: static thumbnail cards (3-col grid) instead of text-only links
- Next project: single full-width card with thumbnail, remove "Previous" link
- Add `--space-section: 120px` to globals.css for section gaps
- Add `.related-thumbnail` CSS class for hover effect (avoids Tailwind vs inline conflict)

---

## Phase 3: Strip Card Chrome

**Why:** Every reference has thumbnails floating in space — no borders, shadows, or dramatic desaturation.

**File:** `components/VideoThumbnail.tsx`

- Remove `boxShadow: 'inset 0 0 0 1px #141414'` from both mobile + desktop

## Phase 4: Simplify Project Card Text

**Why:** Electric Theatre shows image + title only. Save descriptions for detail pages.

**File:** `components/ProjectCard.tsx`

- Title: `Lora italic` → `Inter 400`, reduce size from `clamp(22px, 2.2vw, 28px)` → `clamp(18px, 1.8vw, 24px)`
- Remove `gridDescription` display entirely
- Keep client as small uppercase metadata below title

---

## Phase 5: Spacing + CSS Polish

**File:** `app/globals.css`

- Add `--space-section: 120px` after `--space-2xl`
- Add `.related-thumbnail` + `.group:hover .related-thumbnail` classes for related work hover

---

## NOT Touched

- Perception system
- lib/projects.ts (no data model changes)

- View transitions

## Verification
